decision: ms and s are lexer suffixes, like deg. A bare number in a time position means seconds. Whole sub-second milliseconds print as Nms. Everything else prints as seconds. clip: prints after each.

decision: Anims sit in a side table on the module, copied on use like styles. They are not values. play looks the name up there. clip == idle therefore still sees idle as a word.

decision: Keys are evenly spaced unless at: gives fractions of the key duration, from 0 to 1, nondecreasing. The default is uniform Catmull-Rom with duplicated ends. ease replaces that spline. Numbers, angles, vectors, and sizes move in value space. Colors move in OKLab. Words, components, and booleans step. Any other kind is E0320.
why: One interpolation per kind, and no guess. A 0 to 360 spin passes through the intermediates. Ease does not stack on the spline.

decision: Node identity is the key the existing seed mixer hashes. This change does not rewrite node_seed, line-numbered let seeds, or fx argument seeding.
why: The other task owns author-controlled seed keys. This task owns when that key changes. The count pass and the draw pass still have to agree, because a flipped pick renames a node.

decision: Scope addressing is the base. A name hangs from its file, def, or slot, not from the groups around it. An explicit name whose instance is unnamed is an error. Patches name declared names only. The seed mixer stays.
why: The judge scored this shape 19 to 8. The other shape puts every ancestor name in the key, which is the monk head-grain move. The unnamed-instance hole in the base would still renumber name:shaft, so that case is an error instead.

decision: Every call of a def that contains a name is named. The torii group that shared beam with its curve is nuki_parts, and @beam still names the curve. The spec describes scope keys, patch hops, and positional-seed.
why: A group in the key moved the monk head grain. An unnamed call that holds a name would renumber that name when a sibling draw is inserted.

decision: A copy hop stays on that copy, a drawn index that matches nothing is E0340, and a stable key outside the check scope keeps its full key in the fix. The play prepass registers each repeat and grid copy.
why: Both reviews found silent retargets. A hop through copy 1 could land on copy 0, and a missing index was dropped.

decision: A final star lists every copy's children. A def that reuses a shape word is a component. An unnamed call still has @self. An off instance still admits a hop through it. An entry-file let that binds a shape word stays out of the static check.
why: Codex found four misses against the spec. Each one dropped a patch or a check the rules already required.

decision: A path under an off instance or slot is checked through every declared hop. An empty slot fallback is an empty scope. Draw-site rand stays file, key, and a counter. An unnamed key still follows its tree parent, and the contract says so.
why: Codex reviewed beef76e. Three findings were silent misses. Two were the spec saying something the mixer and the unnamed key do not do. The mixer stays.

decision: Render on the GPU (Skia Ganesh on Metal) by default, fall back to CPU when none is available, and let [build] backend or --backend force either. The cache key and the determinism rule gain the resolved backend.
why: A full clean chibi build fell from 33.5s on CPU to 6.6s on Metal. GPU output may differ from CPU output and between machines, and the owner accepted that. backend = "cpu" keeps one backend for consistency.
evidence: chibi release build, median of 5 in the prototype; this change: ref 33.47s, cpu 33.53s, gpu 7.07s and 6.58s, auto 6.71s. cpu bytes equal d4f21bb, two gpu builds equal

decision: A bad name is one E0312. A star with no declared part is E0340. An anim reports each full path. @self stays hidden until checks. A shared outer loop and a slot keep the current copy, and an index counts the loops still open.
why: Codex reviewed 0616a59. Each finding dropped a diagnostic or a copy the spec already required.

decision: A grid cell's translation is applied to the records it registered, including names inside those records. A single inner copy keeps the outer loop's skipped index. The manifest checks field stays the C diagnostics.
why: Codex reviewed f67ba84. Grid copies measured the same point. The one-copy branch dropped the index the many-copy branch kept. The spec had widened checks past what the manifest writes.

decision: profile: accepts vector, svg, raster, or auto on every target. An unknown word or a non-word value is E0206. An explicit profile:vector or profile:svg on a .png or .gif target is E0206. A manifest vector or svg default still lets raster targets build. Any other manifest profile is E0200 once, at its line in artscript.toml.
why: A raster target cannot honor a vector profile, so an explicit one is an author mistake. A project-wide default must not break every .png target (#22).

decision: A manifest error points at the line and column of the bad value or the TOML syntax error, not 1:1. A project, defaults, lint or build key that is not a table is E0200 instead of being ignored.
why: An author fixes a manifest by its line. Ignoring a section of the wrong type dropped the author's settings with no error.
evidence: issue #23; manifest_errors_point_at_the_bad_line; artscript check on [lint] raw-color = "loud" now prints 5:13

decision: The guard divergence error of the play prepass is E0344. E0343 stays a reference, patch, or check that resolves to several nodes. Entry-file plays apply by position: the line and copy index of each enclosing loop, then the play line. A play in a def body keeps evaluation order, and an entry-file play that reaches the same node still wins, because the outer scope wins.
why: PR 18 and PR 19 both claimed E0343, and PR 19 landed first. PR 18 applied a def-body play after every entry play. PR 19 lets the outer scope win for channels as for static patches, and that rule is the consistent one.

decision: A PNG samples tapered strokes at its own scale, so name.png is the same with or without @2x. An SVG samples at the target's highest scale and a GIF at 1. The build evaluates the target once per distinct sample scale and reports diagnostics from the highest-scale evaluation only.
why: Adding scale:1,2 changed the bytes of the 1x PNG, because every PNG was rendered from one scene sampled at the highest scale.

decision: A let, if, each, or play statement seeds from its tag among its siblings (let y~1), counted like an unnamed draw. An anim duration seeds from the anim name, and a patch from the anim name and its path count. The line is no longer part of any seed.
why: A comment, a blank line, or artscript fmt moved a let y = rand(...). Draws already seeded from the key and did not move.
evidence: issue #39; comments_and_blank_lines_keep_statement_seeds; artscript build before and after fmt both print matrix(1 0 0 1 128 211.186)

decision: A part whose name starts with _ is private to its def. A patch or anim path that names it from an instance block is E0340 that says the part is private. A final * skips it, and the E0340 names note leaves it out. Entry-file _ names stay patchable. @_name still resolves in the def body.
why: Every name: in a def was a patch target, so renaming a part a def names only for copy @part broke callers. The _ prefix already meant private to use.

decision: A def instance is an isolated group, like a layer. A blend inside the def, erase included, stays inside the instance. A blend on the call composites the finished instance onto the caller. group stays the only pass-through group. The renderer gives every instance its own layer.
why: An instance was a plain group, so blend:erase in a def erased the caller's art, and a:.99, an effect, a mask, or a clip on the call changed the blend result. Skipping the layer when no child blends is not byte-neutral: it moved existing layer outputs by up to 45 levels, so it was not adopted.
evidence: issue #47; a_def_instance_keeps_its_blend_modes_inside_it; chibi rebuild changes PNGs by at most 4 levels per channel

decision: `artscript docs` prints a short core card and a topic index. `artscript docs <topic>...` prints the card and those topic files from docs/topics/. The skill lists the topics and reads the card and its topics in one call.
why: An agent paid for the whole 4,608-token card in every session and re-read it on every turn. Edits need one or two topics. A second docs call costs a turn, so one call prints both.
evidence: local artbench, 8 runs per arm, interleaved: cost -10.3% [-15.9%, -4.1%], cache write -15.1%, turns, duration, judge and checks within noise

decision: A `ramp` or `color` row name inside a palette may be any reserved word, keywords included, and an expression member segment may be a keyword. Bindings, def parameters, and draw verbs still reject reserved words with E0105.
why: A row name is only read qualified (`shroom.backdrop`), so it cannot collide with a keyword or a future word. Agents writing `color backdrop` got E0105 and a failed check for no benefit. Keywords need no lexer change, only a member-segment arm.

decision: Nesting under a shape clips the children to the shape's geometry (antialiased, its own fill rule), not to its painted alpha. fill, stroke, alpha, and blur: on the shape do not change the clip. The shape and its children stay one isolated group on every backend, so SVG now writes isolation:isolate on a shape with children. fx outline adds each child's area intersected with the shape's geometry, except under an opaque fill, which already covers it.
why: Children composited source-atop on the shape's pixels, so a fill:none shape hid them with no diagnostic and a 30% shape drew opaque children at 30%. Geometry clipping gives fill:none clip frames for tiles, atlases, and wrapped backgrounds, keeps opaque details on glass, ice, and membranes, matches inside @x, and matches the SVG clipPath that was already written.
evidence: issue #54; a_fill_none_parent_still_clips_and_shows_its_children; an_opaque_child_of_a_translucent_parent_stays_opaque; outline_traces_the_children_a_fill_none_parent_shows; nesting_under_a_translucent_shape_matches_inside; chibi and slime rebuilds change PNGs only along nesting shapes' antialiased edges (up to 68 levels, the child now covers the edge pixel at the clip's coverage) and on the strawberry's translucent dewdrop (up to 73 levels), whose highlights are no longer faded; outlining every child under an opaque fill raised alpha on the outline's outer rim by up to 133 levels, so it is skipped there

decision: A measurement of an @ref outside a check reads the bounding box of the target in the current local frame: the inverse of the current transform maps it from canvas coordinates. A check still measures in canvas coordinates.
why: Inside a def or an offset group, @a.top.y returned the canvas value while at: is local, so at:@a.top.x,@a.top.y applied the instance offset twice. The anchor o workaround undid only translation, so a mirrored or rotated instance drew misplaced parts with no error.

decision: Each branch of an expression if takes a tight tuple, so if k < 2 then 3,4 else 5,6 picks one of two points. A tuple that starts with an if now needs parentheses: (if c then a else b),3. fmt prints those parentheses and drops the ones around a branch tuple.
why: Issue 56: fmt removed the parentheses from then (3,4) else (5,6) and the file stopped parsing, and authors wrote then k*32,200 else 576,300 by hand and got expected else. One rule for both branches beats a then that takes a tuple and an else that does not. Two checked-in files used else x,width for (if ...),width and were rewritten with parentheses.

decision: A built-in verb given more positional items than it reads is E0321 at the statement. The message names the verb, how many items it takes, and the first extra item. rect, grid, or ellipse with a number and then extra items gets the fix `rect w,h`. The values topic says a vector w,h is a size.
why: Extra items were evaluated and dropped, so rect w x h drew a w by w square with no diagnostic. Components already rejected extra items with E0321.
evidence: issue #55; extra_positional_items_on_a_builtin_verb_are_e0321; a_vector_is_a_size_and_filtered_words_still_pass; examples/chibi and examples/slime still check clean

decision: off-canvas (L0102) measures a shape after its clips and masks. Its bounds are cut to every inside path and node mask on it and its groups, each grown by three feather sigmas. outside, inverted masks, and field masks cut nothing. This replaces skipping every group with a clip.
why: A masked autotile warned once per tile and build refused to write, though the mask kept every pixel on the canvas. The old rule also hid content an outside clip or a large inside path left off the canvas.

decision: docs/semantics.md is removed. The author card is docs/language.md and the files in docs/topics/. A behavior change does not have to edit every write-up in the same change, and the write-ups do not have to be reconciled with each other.
why: The long notes, the card, and the topics had to stay in agreement. The notes were a second spec, and the compiler never read them.

decision: fx outline draws the union of its areas, filled and stroked at 2 * width, at the outline color's own alpha, and erases it inside every translucent area: a fill or stroke with a stop below alpha 1, or a descendant with a: below 1. The outlined node's own a: still fades the whole node. Children add areas only under a shape whose fill shows nothing. SVG writes the ink opaque in a group with the color's opacity and masks it out of translucent areas, and outline paths keep their even-odd fill rule.
why: The ink alpha was multiplied by each area's coverage and every area was drawn behind the content, so a 50% fill got a 50% ring and showed ink through itself, and a translucent outline color darkened where areas overlapped. Glass, ice, ghosts, and wings need a translucent body with a solid outline.
evidence: issue #57; outline_ring_keeps_its_alpha_around_a_translucent_fill; outline_shows_nothing_inside_a_translucent_fill; outline_around_translucent_children_keeps_its_alpha; svg_outline_on_a_translucent_fill_is_not_faded; outline_ring_is_round keeps its exact values; repro pixel 11,32 goes from 60,42,42,128 to 59,42,42,255 and 32,32 from 105,135,166,192 to the bare fill 128,183,229,128 on cpu and gpu; chibi and slime rebuilds change PNGs with no translucent area by at most 2 premultiplied levels (layer rounding), and moss_monk (beads) and sweet_strawberry (dewdrop) by up to 63 and 75 where ink no longer shows through; slime GIFs, with no translucent area, change by up to 47 because their one NeuQuant palette is retrained from every frame; two rebuilds are byte-identical; Chrome renders the new SVG mask to the PNG's pixels
